records.title: Maps and GIS
records.header: T GIS 311 Maps and GIS (6) NSc, RSN
records.text: T GIS 311 Maps and GIS (6) NSc, RSN Introduction to map interpretation and basic spatial analysis through the use of geographic information systems (GIS). Emphasizes developing, through hands-on experience, a fundamental understanding of GIS and the technical expertise necessary for applying GIS in a variety of scenarios such as environmental science, urban planning, nursing, social work, and business. Course overlaps with: BIS 344.

records.title: Intermediate GIS
records.text: T GIS 312 Intermediate GIS (6) NSc Examines GIS techniques that range from spatial analysis using vector and raster data models, to the analysis of three dimensional surfaces in urban space. Prerequisite: T GIS 311.

records.title: Applied GIS and Project Design
records.header: T GIS 313 Applied GIS and Project Design (3) NSc
records.text: T GIS 313 Applied GIS and Project Design (3) NSc Exposes real-world applications of geographic information systems. Discussion centers on the implantation of a GIS and strategies students might take as they begin planning for their own GIS project. Prerequisite: T GIS 311.

records.title: Advanced Applications of GIS
records.header: T GIS 414 Advanced Applications of GIS (5) NSc
records.text: T GIS 414 Advanced Applications of GIS (5) NSc Applies GIS techniques through case studies of social, economic, and environmental issues in the Puget Sound region. Introduces new techniques in basic programming for GIS, using ArcGIS ModelBuilder, and the advanced use of GPS devices. Prerequisite: T GIS 312; T GIS 313.

records.title: Critical Theory and GIS Practicum
records.header: T GIS 415 Critical Theory and GIS Practicum (5) NSc
records.text: T GIS 415 Critical Theory and GIS Practicum (5) NSc Explores the foundational debates that have impacted the evolution of geospatial software, technique, and methodology. Concurrent with these readings and discussions, projects designed in T GIS 313 are fully implemented and results are prepared for digital and print presentation. Prerequisite: T GIS 312; T GIS 313.

records.title: Participatory Mapping
records.text: T GIS 450 Participatory Mapping (5) Introduces students to the goals, principles, methods, and tools associated with participatory mapping. Learn how to collect data directly from community members using a wide range of mapping techniques from digital to tangible mediums.

records.title: Cartography and Data Visualization
records.header: T GIS 460 Cartography and Data Visualization (5) RSN
records.text: T GIS 460 Cartography and Data Visualization (5) RSN Introduce students to the interpretation and representation of spatial information. Learn to analyze and create persuasive, beautiful maps and data visualizations. Course overlaps with: BIS 343. Prerequisite: T GIS 311
